question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

To smell a rat

options.text: To have reason to know the presence of a rat
To know the smell of a rat
To learn the smell of a rat

solution:
The correct answer is option 2), i.e., "to have reason to suspect ."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let’s look at the meaning of the given idiom/ phrase: 
 
• The phrase 'To smell a rat' means 'To suspect that something is wrong or not quite right.' (यह संदेह करना कि कुछ गलत है या बिल्कुल सही नहीं है)
 
• *Example*:
 
 
• *​I only began to **smell a rat** when he couldn't come up with the documents he claimed to have.*
 
 
 
• Hence, the only possible answer is option 2, 'to have reason to suspect ,' which exactly resembles the meaning of the given idiom/ phrase.
